How I judge content

A brand I study
Presello — real estate, Philippines

What I admire is how they turn real estate, usually a dry and transactional topic, into genuinely watchable YouTube content — blending property showcases with storytelling and personality instead of just listing features. It's the standard I hold content to: built for engagement, not just information.

Background

Before VA + automation

Years in BPO / call center work with international clients, which is where the day-to-day habits underneath everything above actually came from.

Multitasking under pressure Clear client communication Same-day issue resolution US-hours reliability

From the Call Floor to the Control Panel

Before automation and content calendars, my day-to-day was a customer service floor — years across technical support, sales, and retail accounts for international clients. Every call was a different problem: walking someone through a broken device, closing a sale before the customer hung up, or calming a frustrated shopper who wanted an answer five minutes ago. I learned to think fast, stay calm under pressure, and explain things clearly no matter how heated the conversation got.

What I didn't expect was how much of that would transfer. Managing a queue of impatient callers isn't so different from managing a content calendar with a deadline every day. Solving a technical issue on the fly is the same instinct I now use to debug a broken automation. And the patience it takes to walk a non-technical customer through a fix is exactly what it takes to explain, in plain language, why a missed-call automation matters to a business owner who's never touched a CRM.

When I started teaching myself AI automation and prompt engineering, it didn't feel like starting over — it felt like pointing years of client-facing pressure-testing at a new set of tools. I built my first GoHighLevel workflows to solve problems I recognized instantly from the call floor: leads going cold, follow-ups falling through, no one answering fast enough. That's the throughline from customer service to VA and automation work — I'm still solving the same problem, just earlier in the process, before it ever reaches a frustrated customer on the other end of the line.
